episode.source_question: When nested transaction.atomic() blocks exit, what has actually committed, what can still roll back, and when do transaction.on_commit() callbacks run?

title: Where to place a transactional outbox handoff
question: Where should a Django application place an outbox write and its dispatch trigger so nested transaction.atomic() rollback semantics are respected, dispatch starts only after the outer commit, and the remaining delivery gap is explicit?

claims.title: Inner success remains provisional until outer success
claims.statement: Rows written and callbacks registered by a successful inner block can still be removed by a later rollback of an enclosing savepoint or the outer transaction.

claims.title: `on_commit()` callbacks follow their rollback scope
claims.statement: Registration captures active savepoint IDs, so rollback prunes callbacks from that scope while callbacks from surviving sibling or outer scopes remain queued.

claims.title: Surviving callbacks run after commit and autocommit restoration
claims.statement: After the outer body exits without error and commit succeeds, __exit__ restores autocommit and drains surviving callbacks in registration order before returning; callback code can therefore query or start a new transaction.

claims.title: Treat `on_commit()` as a post-commit handoff, not a delivery guarantee
claims.statement: The useful design signal is to place side effects after transaction success, while recognizing that this in-process queue supplies no durable retry or crash-recovery contract.

facts.statement: A successful connection commit arms queued hooks for the later autocommit transition; rollback clears the whole queue.
Rolling back a savepoint removes callbacks whose registration snapshot contains that savepoint ID; releasing a savepoint does not run them.
Inside an atomic block, on_commit stores the callback with the set of active savepoint IDs; outside a transaction in autocommit mode, it executes immediately.
set_autocommit(True) updates backend and connection state before running and clearing the armed callback queue.
Django tests keep callbacks silent through nested success and observe them only after the outer block commits.

Django tests discard callbacks and rows from rolled-back savepoints, preserve successful siblings, discard everything on outer rollback, and show savepoint=False failure dooming its enclosing transaction scope.

uncertainties.statement: The in-memory callback queue does not establish delivery if the process exits after database commit but before or during callback execution.

design_statements.title: Place the row and registration inside the owning rollback scope
design_statements.statement: Create the outbox row at the application-service boundary that owns the business mutation, using the same active atomic(using=alias) scope and database alias. Before that rollback scope exits, register transaction.on_commit(lambda: wake(outbox_id), using=alias). An inner or outer rollback then removes both the row and the callback registration; only a successful outer commit allows the callback to run. The callback is a latency optimization. Independently scanning pending rows is the recovery path.

design_statements.title: Application-service mutation boundary
design_statements.statement: Insert the outbox row beside the business write inside the same atomic(using=alias) block and on the same alias, so both writes share every enclosing savepoint and the outer commit.

design_statements.title: Post-commit wake-up
design_statements.statement: After the row has an ID and before the current transaction or savepoint scope exits, register transaction.on_commit(lambda: wake(outbox_id), using=alias). If registration happens after the owning transaction has exited, on_commit() executes immediately and no longer provides ordering against that commit.

design_statements.title: Recovery dispatcher
design_statements.statement: Independently scan pending outbox rows and retry unfinished publication. Use the outbox ID as a stable deduplication key, and define explicitly when a row becomes delivered. Treat on_commit() only as a low-latency wake-up for this recovery path.

design_statements.title: Inner rollback
design_statements.statement: The outbox row is rolled back and the callback registration from that savepoint scope is pruned.

design_statements.title: Inner success followed by outer rollback
design_statements.statement: The provisional outbox row is rolled back later and the queued callback never runs.

design_statements.title: Successful outer commit
design_statements.statement: The transaction commits the outbox row, Django restores autocommit, and the surviving wake-up callback then runs.

design_statements.title: Process exit after commit but before callback completion
design_statements.statement: The committed pending row remains, the fast wake-up may be lost, and independent scanning is required to resume publication.

design_statements.title: Commit-to-callback gap
design_statements.statement: Django does not guarantee that an in-process callback completes after commit. In this proposed design, process exit can therefore leave a committed pending outbox row without the fast wake-up; only independent scanning can recover it.

design_statements.title: Publish-to-record gap
design_statements.statement: If the dispatcher publishes an event and exits before recording completion, a retry may publish it again. Broker acknowledgement, mark-delivered ordering, and consumer deduplication were not inspected.

design_statements.title: Exact application edit points were not inspected
design_statements.statement: This framework episode contains no application service, outbox schema, broker adapter, or dispatcher, so it cannot name a project file or establish retry and idempotency behavior.

design_statements.title: Rollback scopes
design_statements.statement: Prove that inner rollback and outer rollback after inner success leave neither the outbox row nor a runnable callback.

design_statements.title: Commit order
design_statements.statement: Prove that outer commit makes the row visible before the wake-up callback runs.

design_statements.title: Lost wake-up
design_statements.statement: Suppress the callback and prove that independent scanning still finds and publishes the pending row.

design_statements.title: Duplicate publication
design_statements.statement: Crash after publish but before completion recording and prove that retry does not create an unintended duplicate effect.

relations.statement: Because inner success remains provisional, the durable row must share the business write's enclosing transaction.
The callback is useful as a post-commit wake-up only when it is registered before the owning transaction exits.
The callback crash window makes independent scanning the recovery path.
